batch_strategy: Choose missing condition contrasts that distinguish scaffold-specific solvent responses from loading associations and isolated row variation. Follow the new ether-arene and strong-eluent finish findings with matched loading experiments, constrain transfer across carbonyl and nitrogen environments, and test one conspicuous predicted solvent-response reversal. All 32 supplied point predictions are frozen verbatim in the reasons before any new label reveal.

hypotheses.content: Weak-eluent responses of aryl ethers depend on substitution and accompanying functional groups. The new m116 and m123 50/1 observations differ substantially despite both having two methoxy groups, although their different amounts prevent assigning the contrast entirely to structure.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Crossed loading extensions and intermediate solvent anchors can teach graph-condition interactions and prevent one ether-family retention offset from spreading across structurally distinct rows.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does the m116/m123 contrast persist at opposite loading extremes, and do their intermediate curves and the m87 ester curve require different solvent slopes?

hypotheses.content: Weak-eluent finish growth learned for other aromatic esters may overextend to m56. Its new low-load 100/1 finish is 7.85 mL, versus 9.15 mL at 10/1; the modest measured decrease does not by itself establish a reproducible turnover or its mechanism.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: A solvent-gap point and an amount contrast can distinguish a learnable boundary from an isolated endpoint and constrain extrapolation across the many ester rows.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Is the 40/1 finish elevated at the same amount, and does the short 100/1 response persist at higher loading?

hypotheses.content: Strong-eluent finish plateaus are scaffold-specific and may depend on loading. At middle loading, m197 retains a roughly 25–28 mL finish from pure EA through 5/1, whereas methoxy-substituted salicylaldehyde m117 has a much shorter pure-EA finish. Hydrogen-bonding explanations remain chemical possibilities rather than established mechanisms.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The model needs separate onset and finish responses conditioned on graph environment; a generic contraction toward pure EA fails for at least the measured m197 loading context.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does m197's pure-EA plateau persist across amounts, and do the two brominated salicylaldehyde environments share it?

hypotheses.content: Aryl-ketone finish responses depend jointly on substitution, solvent ratio and loading. The new m32 1/1 labels support short finishes there, while its higher-load finishes increase at 2/1 and 5/1 but decrease relative to lower loading at 50/1. m33 and fused ketone m182 supply different strong-eluent finish patterns, so a family-wide offset is inadequate.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Local curves and amount contrasts can repair endpoint-specific interpolation while constraining transfer across closely related aromatic carbonyl graphs.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Where do amount-associated finish differences change with solvent strength, and which strong-eluent finish regimes persist into pure EA?

hypotheses.content: Amount associations vary by chemical environment, solvent ratio and endpoint. Several alcohol and cyclic-ester contrasts primarily shift onset, while biphenyl supplies a finish-dominant contrast and dibenzylamine shows a different local regime. These are associations in recorded conditions, not established causal amount effects.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The predictor remains nearly amount-invariant for many selected contrasts. Matched labels can teach distinct V1 and V2 interactions across common row families.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: At which solvent ratios do onset- or finish-associated amount differences appear, and how do those boundaries change across OH, amine, cyclic-ester and hydrocarbon environments?

hypotheses.content: For m72, the combination of loading solvent and loading-solvent volume may affect retention locally even when sample amount matches. At 5/1, lower-load DCM/200 uL and PE/300 uL records have different finishes, whereas high-load 10/1 finishes are similar. The separate contributions of solvent identity and solvent volume are not identified.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The selected pair tests whether the encoded loading-context fields need solvent-ratio-specific interactions beyond density-times-sample-volume loading.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: At middle loading and 5/1, do DCM/200 uL and PE/300 uL produce distinguishable endpoints despite almost identical predictions?

hypotheses.content: Weak-eluent finish growth and its loading association are scaffold-dependent. The new m198 50/1 high-load finish is close to its middle-load finish, weakening the predicted shorter-finish extrapolation at higher amount. Para-nitro aldehyde and nitro ketone references may have different loading responses at 20/1.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Completing selected amount contrasts constrains when large V2 growth transfers across nitro-carbonyl environments and when an amount correction should remain local.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do 20/1 finishes remain stable across amounts for m198, and do m193 and m37 follow the same association or diverge?

feedback_interpretation: The latest m202 results substantially weaken the previous expectation that its large middle-load 10/1 response extends to higher loading. The high-load endpoint was only 4.62/9.38 mL, versus 35.08/70.35 mL at middle loading and 14.79/21.41 mL at lower loading. Both new 5/1 finishes were near 13.1 mL. This leaves a sharply localized interaction or unexplained row variation as alternatives and argues against propagating a broad phosphoryl correction. I therefore do not spend this batch on its remaining pure-EA extensions. The m197 pure-EA finish of 26.73 mL supports the proposed plateau instead of the predicted collapse; the next useful questions are amount dependence and structural transfer. Opposite historical errors for m116 and m123 at 50/1 expose a useful structural contrast, but their different amounts require crossed loading labels before interpreting it. Current predictions have already moved toward those observations, so the selections test transfer after that update rather than claiming the old errors persist. The m56 100/1 result weakens its extrapolated finish growth and motivates a nearby solvent anchor plus an amount contrast. New m32 labels localize its short finish regime at 1/1 while retaining the solvent-dependent loading interpretation at 2/1 and 5/1. Several recent alcohol, amine and ordinary strong-eluent predictions were comparatively close, favoring targeted missing contrasts over repeating those measured tuples.
batch_rationale: The batch uses the full supplied pool to target missing relationships with explicit measured references. Crossed ether-arene loading experiments follow the strongest new structural contrast while controlling its main recorded confound. Strong-eluent boundary experiments test the confirmed m197 plateau, its brominated analogues, and distinct aryl-ketone finish behavior. Intermediate solvent points connect these boundaries to measured curves and limit overgeneralization of local corrections. Alcohol, amine, cyclic-ester and biphenyl contrasts ask whether loading changes onset, finish, or both; the m72 pair separately tests two recorded loading contexts whose individual solvent and volume effects cannot be disentangled. Nitro-carbonyl extensions constrain transfer of weak-eluent finish responses across amounts. The m16 pair explores a predicted onset reversal in a common acrylate family without treating that prediction as an observed failure. These coordinated labels should improve graph-condition interactions and separate V1/V2 learning across the Row-distribution. No selection is intended to maximize retention or improve the selected separation itself. Historical acquisition errors guide follow-up but are not current-model residuals; V2 minus V1 remains an elution interval, and single-predictor quantile spans are not treated as calibrated epistemic uncertainty.
